findings.title: BaseCalendarService.createEvent signature breaks the Calendar interface contract
findings.body: The Calendar interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts was changed to require `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`. The BaseCalendarService (this file) is declared as `abstract class BaseCalendarService implements Calendar`, but its createEvent still has signature `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>` and is not marked abstract. TypeScript will error out at build time because the implementation is not assignable to the interface (the missing required `credentialId` parameter). Additionally, concrete CalDAV-derived integrations (Apple Calendar, etc.) inherit this method, so EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents's third argument `destination.externalId` is silently dropped. The base signature must be updated to accept and forward `credentialId` (and likely ignore it where appropriate) for the project to compile and behave correctly.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback uses a self-referential find that can never match
findings.body: Line 256 reads `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined (truthy is false), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. `cal.externalId === undefined`. That condition is false for any real calendar (externalIds are real strings), so the find returns undefined and `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined. The previous code used a plain `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Net effect: updateEvent currently passes `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update` (and the subsequent `events.patch` at line 168/277) instead of either `primary` or the booking's actual destination calendar externalId. That's a regression from the single-destinationCalendar behavior and is likely to produce 400/404 errors or update the wrong calendar. The same tautological pattern is duplicated at line 317 in `deleteEvent`, where `selectedCalendar` falls back to the local `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` — meaning cancellations without a propagated externalCalendarId will try to delete from "primary" and may delete the wrong event.

findings.title: Legacy cancellation fallback runs once per reference, producing N×M extra delete calls
findings.body: The new code at lines 422-484 wraps both the credentialId-keyed path and the legacy fallback (no `credentialId`) inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For any booking with multiple calendar references that lack `credentialId` (i.e. bookings created before the reference→credentialId migration), the legacy branch executes for EACH reference: it fetches ALL user calendar credentials and pushes `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` for each. That is N (legacy references) × M (user calendars) extra API calls, and each call sends that iteration's `uid`/`externalCalendarId` to every calendar — these uids correspond to different calendar providers, so the legacy branch will issue delete requests for an event ID on calendars where it never existed (and may 404). The original (pre-PR) code only invoked the legacy fallback once per cancellation. Move the legacy fallback outside of the per-reference loop and only iterate once with the original reference's uid/externalCalendarId, or guard the loop so legacy deletions only happen once per booking.

findings.title: Booking record only stores the first host's destinationCalendar for collective events
findings.body: When writing the new Booking row, only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is used (`destinationCalendar: { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } }`). For collective events the PR explicitly pushes every team member's `destinationCalendar` into the array (lines around 1074-1078), so multiple hosts each get their own calendar event via EventManager.create — but the Booking row ends up linked to only the organizer/first host's destination calendar. Later operations that read `booking.destinationCalendar` (handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156, payments webhook.ts:101-119, the booking reminder cron at bookingReminder.ts:107-130, etc.) will only see one of several destinations and may therefore miss cancellations, reminders, or webhooks for other hosts. The BookingReferences table mitigates the calendar delete path, but anything keyed on `booking.destinationCalendar` (emails, webhooks, cron reminders, refund flows) silently drops the rest.

findings.title: Read of `integration` on potentially-undefined destination calendar can throw
findings.body: Line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without first checking if `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is defined: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. The destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty (which is exactly the case the Google Meet fallback is meant to handle, since non-team or no-destination flows now produce `null`). Accessing `.integration` on undefined throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the request fails before the location is rewritten to Cal Video. The check should be `!mainHostDestinationCalendar || mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: Empty firstName/lastName fields added to team member objects
findings.body: The team-member promise at lines 986-1000 now sets `firstName: ""` and `lastName: ""` in the returned object. The TeamMember/CalendarEvent.team.members TypeScript type (in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) does not declare these keys, so they are extra/missing properties on every team attendee. They will be ignored by CalendarService implementations today, but they leak into the persisted meeting attendee list on every external calendar (e.g. ICS attendee fields, Google Meet attendee payloads generated by translateAttendees in larkcalendar/office365). The change is undocumented in the PR description and can interact with downstream consumers that expect only the documented TeamMember shape.

findings.title: Organizer email may be overridden by undefined main destination calendar
findings.body: Inside the attendees payload at line 122: `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`. When the array is empty the optional chain resolves to undefined and the fallback correctly uses `organizer.email`, so this is fine for the empty-array path. However, for collective events with multiple destinations where the chosen `mainHostDestinationCalendar` lacks an `externalId` (e.g. a DestinationCalendar row created without one), the code silently falls back to the organizer's email and Google will reject/lose the organizer mapping. There's no distinction between "no destination" and "destination missing externalId".

findings.title: createAttendees only adds attendees to the first destination calendar
findings.body: In `createEvent` at line 128 the first host's calendar is selected for the event, then `createAttendees` (line 164) re-selects the same first element. The catch path at line 158 (`await this.deleteEvent(eventId, event, calendarId)`) cleans up by deleting from `calendarId` (the first). For a collective event whose other hosts' calendars the EventManager separately creates via createAllCalendarEvents, those other events will not have attendees attached at all (organizer + invitees included) because Lark's createAttendees only runs inside this one createEvent call. The destinationCalendar → attendee invite propagation described in the PR for collective bookings is not actually implemented for Lark.

findings.title: destinationCalendar built from booking.destinationCalendar falls back to user.destinationCalendar unsafely
findings.body: The expression `booking?.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []` will wrap a single `DestinationCalendar` row in an array. Downstream `EventManager.create(evt)` will then process only that one destination, ignoring the user-level `user.destinationCalendar` even when the booking actually intended to be a team/collective booking with multiple destinations. For collective events that require confirmation, the hosts that are not represented in `booking.destinationCalendar` will not be invited when the organizer confirms. Confirm `booking.eventType.schedulingType === COLLECTIVE` and append the team members' destinations (mirroring handleNewBooking.ts ~line 1074) before passing to EventManager.

findings.title: Comment-only change: typo fix is unrelated to the PR
findings.body: The commit changes `orginalBookingDuration` → `originalBookingDuration` in `ensureAvailableUsers`. That's a fine cleanup, but it isn't mentioned in the PR description and isn't related to the destinationCalendar-array refactor. Mixing unrelated typo fixes into a feature/bugfix PR makes bisecting and reverting harder; either split it into its own commit or document it explicitly.

findings.title: Behavior-preserving spread refactor buried in a destinationCalendar PR
findings.body: Two spread ternaries are rewritten (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and the matching `requestedSlug`). The results are equivalent because `false` is ignored when spreading. This isn't a bug, but the change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be moved to its own commit to keep the diff focused on the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: No tests for a sweeping CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar contract change
findings.body: The PR converts `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across 22 files (every CalendarService implementation, EventManager, Booking/Cancel/Reschedule handlers, webhooks, three trpc handlers, payment webhooks, builders, types) yet adds no unit or integration tests. The author explicitly acknowledges in the checklist that tests were not added. Specific regression surfaces that are not covered: (a) collective COLLECTIVE bookings where multiple destinationCalendars are stored on the evt and propagated through handleNewBooking→EventManager.create→each CalendarService.createEvent with the correct credentialId; (b) cancellation when a booking has multiple bookingReferences with different credentials (the N×M legacy path bug); (c) the calendar-removal credentialId fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent; (d) the BOOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REJECTED / BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook payload shape (only one of three test expectations was updated in webhook.e2e.ts). At minimum, a smoke test exercising collective new-booking/cancel/reschedule end-to-end on the dev stack is warranted before merge.
